## Sequencing-gate update: first half SATISFIED — spec half is merged

项目总监席 · session `session_01KGtaLpkW1mycWgkbSb3H6t`

The gate in this card's body has two halves. As of 2026-08-31:

1. **objectstack#13855's spec PR merged** ✅ — objectstack#13897 landed on objectstack main as squash commit `39404f3d9` (contract review PASS recorded on objectstack#13855; the card is closed completed). Note for verifiers: squash merging makes an ancestor check on the branch head return false — confirm landing by grepping main's log for the PR number, not by ancestry.
2. **objectui has adopted the `@objectstack/*` version carrying it** ❌ — still outstanding. The spec change shipped with a `@objectstack/spec` minor changeset, so it reaches this repo only via a spec release plus a version bump here.

**What the adopted version must carry** (adoption check for the dispatching seat): the shared module `packages/spec/src/shared/section-group-reference.ts` (exports `FIELD_GROUP_KEY_PATTERN`), the `group` key accepted on both section surfaces (page `record:details` sections and view `form.sections`, aliases `fieldGroup`/`groupKey` folded to `group`), and the two reference diagnostics `page-section-group-unknown` / `form-section-group-unknown` in `@objectstack/lint`.

Design facts the renderer half must follow verbatim (from the merged spec, not to be re-derived): group ⊕ fields exactly-one per section; group-owned presentation keys are REFUSED beside `group` (no override semantics); mixed section kinds coexist in declared array order; `group` is banned on wizard steps; resolution goes through `deriveFieldGroupLayout` (ADR-0085 §5) as the single assembler.

Card stays `pm:queue`; do not dispatch until half 2 is verified against the checks above.

## Gate re-measured by the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`): **half cleared, still blocked** → `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`

This card was selected for dispatch this round. Its ⛔ sequencing gate has two conditions, and they have now diverged — so recording the measurement rather than leaving the next round to redo it.

> ⛔ objectstack#13855's spec PR is merged **AND** objectui has adopted the `@objectstack/*` version carrying it.

### Condition 1 — spec PR merged: ✅ **YES**

objectstack#13855 is closed `completed` (2026-08-31T19:16:03Z), and the code is on `objectstack` main (`2bff79ae`). Measured, not inferred from the closure:

| landed | path |
|---|---|
| the shared mixing rule | `packages/spec/src/shared/section-group-reference.ts` |
| view-level section | `FormSectionSchema.group` — `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` |
| record page section | `RecordDetailsProps.sections[].group` — `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` |
| key-grammar single source | `FIELD_GROUP_KEY_PATTERN`, `packages/spec/src/data/field-group-layout.ts` |
| dangling-reference lint | `validate-form-layout.ts` + `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` (+ both test files) |
| spec-side pins | `packages/spec/src/ui/section-group-reference.test.ts` |

⭐ **This also answers the open question in this card's own Deliverable §2.** The card said *"if the spec half lands both surfaces"* — it did. `field-group-layout.ts` says so explicitly: the key *"is now written on TWO surfaces: the group that DECLARES it (`ObjectFieldGroupSchema.key`) and the layout sections that REFERENCE it (`FormSectionSchema.group`, `RecordDetailsProps.sections[].group` — #13855)."* So both consumers are in scope, and the mixing rule is single-sourced in `section-group-reference.ts` — which is also the answer to this card's ⛔ *"no re-implementation of assembly rules on the objectui side."* There is one module to resolve against.

### Condition 2 — objectui adopted a version carrying it: ⛔ **NO**

- `@objectstack/spec` on **objectstack main** is `version: 17.2.0` — read from `packages/spec/package.json` at `2bff79ae`.
- `@objectstack/spec` **resolved by objectui** is `17.2.0` — `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`'@objectstack/spec@17.2.0'`), consistent with PR #7167's independent reading today (*"`@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0 as installed"*) on a fresh head.
- The feature is sitting in an **unconsumed changeset**: `.changeset/section-field-group-reference.md`, *"feat(spec,lint): a layout section can reference a declared field group instead of copying its members (#13855)"*, declared as **"Additive accept widening."**

⇒ The same version number on both sides is not adoption — it is the feature being **merged but not yet released**. Dispatching now would send a developer to consume a form that the installed package does not declare; the honest outcome would be a premise-false report, and the dishonest one would be a hand-rolled reading of the spec source that violates this card's own ⛔.

### Unblock condition — recorded machine-findably, per #7041 / #6653

**Unblock-when:** `@objectstack/spec` resolves to **≥ 17.3.0** in objectui's `pnpm-lock.yaml` **and** `section-group-reference` is present in the installed package.

Checkable in two commands, no judgement required:

```
grep -E "'@objectstack/spec@[0-9]" pnpm-lock.yaml
ls node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist/shared/ | grep section-group-reference
```

The bump is a **minor** (additive accept widening), so `^17.0.0` / `^17.2.0` ranges will take it on the next install — no manifest edit is needed, only the release plus a lockfile refresh.

### Note for whoever takes this when it unblocks

The objectstack half was *"offered for contract review"* (Clause ②) because it widens what the contract accepts. ⭐ **The objectui half is not that.** Consuming a form the spec already declares is renderer work — it does not widen any objectui surface and does not change what objectui's own contracts accept or reject. So this card is dispatchable at **normal tier** when it unblocks; it is not waiting on the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` quota that is currently holding the retirement pile.

Refs: objectstack#13855 (ruled B, 「直接处理b」) · hotcrm#806 · ADR-0085 §5.

## Half-state closed: `pm:queue` → `pm:on-hold` (not `pm:blocked`), gate re-measured 2026-09-03

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`.

Comment [5491765716](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7051#issuecomment-5491765716) declared the transition 「`pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`」 on 2026-09-01 and the **label never moved**. So for two days this card has been telling every dispatch round it is ready while its own body carries a ⛔ gate that refuses it — and it had already burned one seat's selection round once. Closing the half-state now, with the gate re-measured rather than inherited.

### Condition 1 — spec PR merged: ✅ still yes (unchanged, see 5483253848 / 5491765716)

### Condition 2 — objectui has adopted a version carrying it: ⛔ still NO

Measured today against `origin/main` on both repos:

| reading | value | control (must fire, or the zero means nothing) |
|---|---|---|
| objectui `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `@objectstack/spec` | **`17.2.0`** | `client` / `core` / `formula` / `lint` / `sdui-parser` all found, all `17.2.0` — instrument fires |
| objectstack `main` → `packages/spec/package.json` | **`17.2.0`** | — |
| objectstack `main` → `.changeset/section-field-group-reference.md` | **still present, unconsumed** | 772 pending `.changeset/*.md` on main — instrument fires |

⇒ Same version on both sides, changeset unconsumed. The feature is **merged but not released**, exactly as measured on 2026-09-01. Nothing has moved.

### ⚠️ A non-reading that will catch the next round, recorded so it does not

My first probe was the second half of the recorded check — looking for the feature inside the installed package. It returned **0 hits**. Its controls (`dist/shared` entry count, any file mentioning the key-grammar constant) returned **0 as well**, because that checkout has no `node_modules` at all. That is a non-reading, not a negative, and on its own it is indistinguishable from a real absence. ⛔ Do not run the installed-package half of the check without first asserting `node_modules` exists. The lockfile half needs no install and is the one that stands.

### Correction to the target state: `pm:on-hold`, not `pm:blocked`

The earlier comment named `pm:blocked`. On the protocol that is the wrong bucket for this shape, and the difference is not cosmetic — `pm:blocked` is released by the unlock scan when its upstream issue closes, and **this card's upstream issue is already closed**. Filed as blocked, it would be handed straight back to the queue by the next scan, still unbuildable.

The governing rule is the cross-repo one: when a consuming repo takes an upstream by **published package** rather than a git SHA pin, the unlock criterion is *consumer-installable*, not *upstream merged* — and an unreleased fix goes to `pm:on-hold` with a `Restart-when:` written against the consumer's install surface. That is this case exactly: objectui resolves `@objectstack/spec` by version from the lockfile, and the release plus lockfile refresh are human actions no scan can trigger.

### Restart-when (machine-readable; no judgement required)

**Restart-when:** `@objectstack/spec` resolves to a version **≥ 17.3.0** in objectui `pnpm-lock.yaml` **and** the installed package exposes the section-group-reference shared module.

```
git show origin/main:pnpm-lock.yaml | grep -oE "'@objectstack/spec@[0-9][^']*'" | sort -u
ls node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist/shared/ | grep section-group-reference
```

⚠️ The second command is only valid when `node_modules` exists — assert that first, or it is a non-reading (above).

**Restart-touch:** `pnpm-lock.yaml`

### Dispatch shape when it wakes — unchanged and still correct

Recording it here so the restart does not re-derive it: this card is dispatchable at **normal tier** when it unblocks. The objectstack half was Clause ② because it widened what the contract accepts; the objectui half consumes a form the spec already declares, moves no objectui surface, and changes nothing about what objectui's own contracts accept or reject. It is **not** waiting on the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` queue. Resolution goes through `deriveFieldGroupLayout` as the single assembler, and the mixing rule is single-sourced upstream — ⛔ no assembly rules re-implemented on the objectui side.

## The sequencing gate is SATISFIED and has been for some time — off hold, re-scoped to the remaining half

Moved `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`, graded p2.

### The gate, re-measured

This card's gate reads: *"objectstack#13855's spec PR is merged **AND objectui has adopted the `@objectstack/*` version carrying it**."* Last measurement on this card was **2026-09-03**, recorded as NO.

Measured today by the objectui#8497 dev: **`@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0 is installed and declares `group` on `RecordDetailsProps.sections`**, as a fully specified capability resolved through `deriveFieldGroupLayout`. The gate cleared and nobody re-checked it, so this card sat on hold while its precondition was met.

That is a PM failure on my part rather than a gap in this card — the same one that left a p1 unread for four hours today. **A hold whose gate is a measurable condition needs to be re-measured, not just re-read.**

### ⚠️ Half of this card has been delivered under a different number

**PR #8584** (card objectui#8497) implements the **`record:details`** half:

- `sections[].group` resolved through **`deriveFieldGroupDetailSections`** — the same adapter the synthesized default record page uses, so the two bodies agree by construction rather than by coincidence
- ⛔ no re-implementation of assembly rules on the objectui side, per this card's constraint
- an unresolvable group renders nothing and reports once on the console, matching the spec's assignment of existence-checking to lint
- `@object-ui/types` aligned so the shape compiles for a TypeScript author

I dispatched objectui#8497 without seeing this card. The work is sound and is not being redone; what it means is that **this card's deliverable 1 is done on merge, and deliverable 2 is what remains.**

### What is still owed: the `form.sections` half

Measured by the same dev: `plugin-form` reads `field.group`, but **no form-section renderer reads `section.group`**. So the view-level `form.sections` consumer has not been touched.

Whoever takes this:

- ⭐ **PR #8584 is the worked example.** Read it before designing — the resolution path, the console-report-once behaviour for an unresolvable group, and the containment are all settled there. Follow it rather than inventing a second reading; this card's own text says *"follow the spec design, do not invent a divergent reading."*
- ⚠️ **Do not assume the two surfaces are symmetric.** #8584 found that the `record:details` crash fired inside a `useMemo` **above** the section loop, so a per-section error boundary could not catch it and two containment layers were needed. Whether `form.sections` has the same shape is a measurement, not an inference.
- ⚠️ Check whether `@object-ui/types`' form-section type has the same omission `record:details`' did — objectui#8583 records that `RecordDetailsComponentProps.sections[]` omits six spec-declared keys and declares one the spec refuses. **Note that `vitest` was green on the offending literal because it strips types; only `type-check` saw it.**
- ⭐ **Derive your non-regression axis from what a plausible wrong fix would still satisfy, not from the shape of the bug.** On #8497 the axis I supplied — "the well-formed sections still render" — passed under the caricature, because siblings are exactly what a caricature preserves. The discriminating assertion was that the **group-referenced** section renders **its own** members.

### Related

objectui#8497 / PR #8584 (the `record:details` half, and the intent archaeology: the crashing expression traces to `e997708419c1`, 2026-05-01, months *before* objectstack#13855 declared the key — so the throw was never a deliberate refusal) · objectui#8583 (the types omission found by #8584's compile-time pin) · objectstack#13855 (the ruling) · hotcrm#806 (the measured divergence this form retires)

Per my re-scoping comment 5585977300: **deliverable 1 (`record:details`) is done** on PR #8584's merge (card objectui#8497), which resolves `sections[].group` through `deriveFieldGroupDetailSections`. What remains is the view-level half — measured then, and carried into the order: **`plugin-form` reads `field.group`, but no form-section renderer reads `section.group`.**

## The three constraints the order carries hardest

1. ⭐ **PR #8584 is the worked example.** Read it before designing. The resolution path, the report-once behaviour for an unresolvable group, and the containment are settled there. ⛔ Do not invent a second reading — this card's own text says *"follow the spec design, do not invent a divergent reading."*
2. ⚠️ **Do not assume the two surfaces are symmetric.** #8584 found the `record:details` crash fired inside a `useMemo` **above** the section loop, so a per-section error boundary could not catch it and **two** containment layers were needed. Whether `form.sections` has that shape is **a measurement, not an inference.**
3. ⛔ **No assembly rules re-implemented on the objectui side.** Resolution goes through `deriveFieldGroupLayout` (ADR-0085 §5) as the single assembler, and the mixing rule is single-sourced upstream in `packages/spec/src/shared/section-group-reference.ts`.

The merged spec's design facts are quoted into the order verbatim rather than re-derived: **group ⊕ fields exactly-one per section; group-owned presentation keys REFUSED beside `group` (no override semantics); mixed section kinds coexist in declared array order; `group` banned on wizard steps.**

## ⭐ The non-regression axis, from my own recorded failure on the sibling card

On objectui#8497 the axis I supplied — *"the well-formed sections still render"* — **passed under the caricature**, because sibling sections are exactly what a caricature preserves. The discriminating assertion was that the **group-referenced** section renders **its own members**. That correction is in this order as a requirement, not a suggestion.

⚠️ Also carried: check whether `@object-ui/types`' form-section type has the omission objectui#8583 records for `RecordDetailsComponentProps.sections[]` — and note that **`vitest` was green on the offending literal because it strips types; only `type-check` saw it.**

## Tier

**Normal tier.** The objectstack half was Clause ② because it widened what the contract accepts; the objectui half consumes a form the spec already declares, moves no objectui surface, and changes nothing about what objectui's contracts accept or reject. ⛔ Not waiting on `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

Dispatch order follows in the next comment.
